subject: Arrange identities remain distinct from Mixer ordinals in plug-in inventory and verified writes
question: Can independently named Arrange tracks bind to different Mixer ordinals for occupied parameter writes and empty-slot insertion without using ordinal or duplicate-name rank fallbacks?

reverify.command: On a disposable project, give two Arrange tracks distinct names; put stock Compressor and Channel EQ on one and leave three physical insert slots empty on the other. Open the embedded Mixer in All mode with non-track strips between track strips; refresh the MCP cache, get_inventory by Arrange index and retain its occupied and empty plugin_insert_ref values. In duplicate_applyback mode with the exact disposable project_expected_path, request Compressor threshold 38 percent then its independently read original value, and Channel EQ Peak 1 Gain 3 dB then its independently read original value. Open each occupied editor separately through its exact named strip and read AXValue/AXValueDescription before, after and after restoration. Request Gain insertion through the empty ref after selecting the other track; preserve any first-request State C. If safe_to_retry is true and the slot still reads empty, retry once; independently read the resulting named Gain editor, then reuse the old empty ref to check refusal. Stop the server, quit/discard the disposable project, restore its backup, reopen and verify empty slots and original parameter values.
reverify.expected: Occupied writes bind the independently named Arrange track despite different Mixer ordinals; direct editor reads observe 65 -> 38 -> 65 percent and +2.2 -> +3.0 -> +2.2 dB on this fixture. Wrong occupied-plugin requests and re-used occupied-as-empty refs refuse with write_attempted:false. Preserve, rather than reclassify, a first insert refusal; a successful retry must read Gain at the requested physical slot. Restored fixture reads three empty slots and original parameter values.
reverify.cost: About 10 minutes per locale with Accessibility granted and an owned disposable Logic project

method: Measured the immutable binary carrying commit 0ebf2fa7b70c11f84ed204c50b39e5889eec9c1d (SHA-256 47b929f5dbe9105f1d7828eab7470c263846209b3065d1b488f99e5486fc7125), not a later documentation head. The owned fixture has two distinct synthetic track names. Actual MCP responses were recorded; a separate cfbridge AX reader located the embedded full Mixer by its direct strips, the unique strip by its semantic name field, and the occupied editor by a separately read window title and plug-in static text. That reader only opened/closed occupied editors, never wrote parameters. Slider read failures remain failures. Full raw reads are retained privately; the public receipt contains selected actual responses/readbacks, original artifact hashes and all-slider projection hashes, with only the disposable project path redacted.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This record measures identity association, distinct index spaces, parameter readback, popup geometry and conservative refusal after selection. It does not assert a localized string's origin; the separately derived semantic name-field label is cited to Apple's Name row in the implementation and PR description.

observations.what: Two uniquely named Arrange tracks associated with different full-Mixer ordinals
Occupied Compressor percentage control independently read before write, after write and after inverse write
Occupied Channel EQ first peak-band gain independently read before write, after write and after inverse write
Wrong occupied-plugin identity for the generic parameter operation and wrong occupied plug-in ref for named EQ were rejected before writing
First empty-slot insertion after selecting a different track did not establish the originally acquired binding as stable
One retry with the same track already selected read the requested Gain at physical slot zero and independently opened its named editor
The former empty-slot reference refused after insertion rather than addressing the occupied slot as empty
After stopping the measured server, restoring the owned backup and reopening in Korean, the target chain had three empty physical slots and occupied controls retained their initial values

conclusion: Both occupied verified-write paths used the Arrange identity despite the different Mixer ordinal, and direct editor reads confirmed requested changes and inverse restoration. Empty-slot insertion succeeded only on the single safe retry; the first request stayed State C without slot dispatch. The left-opening popup was anchored by its right edge touching the target slot's left edge, without relaxing remote-menu or unread-target refusal.
limits: Only this Logic 12.3 build 6674 / macOS 26.3 host and this record's UI locale were measured. The reporter's Logic 12.3.1/12.4 reproduction is attributed evidence, not qualification performed here.

This is behavioural measurement, not an E-clean campaign, a film/screenshot qualification, or an audible/rendered audio result. Percentage readback does not establish a dB threshold conversion or exact movement within the one-percentage-point tolerance.

First insertion after changing selected track still refused in both measured locales; the strict original binding was not observed stable. The underlying CF replacement versus AX read failure was not determined, and no fallback or timeout increase was used to manufacture first-request success.

Duplicate/missing names, unread siblings, retained-Mixer ownership, same-name replacement and transient-read recovery are regression-tested with fake AX runtimes, not independently qualified in a live duplicate-name project.

Full raw slider projections are not embedded in this public receipt; their source-file and projection hashes identify the private measurements. Failed slider-description reads were retained and do not establish all controls' semantic identity.
The re-opened restoration was measured in Korean, not independently in every locale. No changes were made to the user's original music project.
